guards_against: _NSSF_EMPLOYEE_CUES had SEVEN third-person members and ZERO person-marked ones, so every -ni- deduction question fell to the 'total' default and doubled the answer (nat_08, live and wrong: TZS 130,000 where the employee share is 65,000)

question: je mwajiri anakukata shilingi ngapi kwenye mshahara wako wa 500000 kwa ajili ya pensheni
guards_against: -ku- (2sg) has ZERO corpus occurrences on this stem. The sweep is structurally blind to it, so this probe is the only evidence it works -- R17's whole point

question: kampuni inamkata dereva kiasi gani kwenye mshahara wa 900000 kwa ajili ya mfuko wa uzeeni

question: tunamukata fundi wetu kiasi gani kwenye mshahara wa 450000 kwa ajili ya pensheni
guards_against: -m- is commonly written -mu- before a consonant. One class member, two spellings -- treating them as two members is how a class gets half-enumerated

question: mwajiri anatukata kiasi gani kwenye mshahara wa 600000 kwa ajili ya mfuko wa hifadhi ya jamii
guards_against: -tu- (1pl) has ZERO corpus occurrences on this stem. Also checks that the bare word 'mwajiri' does not steal the row for the employer branch

question: ninawakata wafanyakazi wangu kiasi gani kwenye mshahara wa 800000 kwa ajili ya pensheni
guards_against: -wa- (cl.2) has ZERO corpus occurrences as an OBJECT on this stem -- the 46 corpus hits attributed to it are all the passive -katwa, a different paradigm

question: nakatwa shilingi ngapi kwenye mshahara wangu wa 550000 kwa ajili ya mfuko wa uzeeni
guards_against: the same absence from the other side: 'anayokatwa' (3sg relative) was a cue and not one person-marked passive form was. ngapi_04 was live and wrong on exactly this shape

question: tunakatwa shilingi ngapi kwenye mshahara wa 400000 kwa ajili ya pensheni
guards_against: 1pl passive. The 2026-08-15 closure fixed subject concord in lists that already had a 1sg member; this list had none, so it was untouched

question: nina wafanyakazi 15 je tozo ya mafunzo inawahusu
guards_against: _APPLICABILITY_CUES held THREE of the five members (-ni-/-ku-/-tu-) on one verb and one tense. -m- and -wa- were absent -- a class the codebase had already started enumerating and then stopped

question: nina wafanyakazi 12 je tozo ya mafunzo itanianza lini
guards_against: the FUTURE host. Only 'ina-' was covered, so 'itanihusu'/'itanianza' missed. nat_04 is this shape and was answered with SDL at 0.5% sourced to NSSF

question: tuna wafanyakazi 11 je tozo ya mafunzo itatuhusu
guards_against: 1pl on the future host -- the intersection of the two paradigms, which is where a per-paradigm closure leaves a hole

question: nina wafanyakazi 6 je tozo ya mafunzo hainihusu
guards_against: the NEGATIVE host. 'does it NOT apply to me' is an applicability question and the answer here is a correct 'it does not' (6 < 10) -- reachable only if the negative host is recognised

question: ni wakati gani mwajiri anatakiwa kuwasilisha michango ya NSSF kwa mwezi
guards_against: waKATi (time) -- 116 corpus rows. A bare `wakat` cue for the -wa- member would read every one of them as an employee-party question

question: je ni halali kumwajiri mfanyakazi bila mkataba wa maandishi
guards_against: MKATaba (employment contract) -- 36 corpus rows. A bare `mkat` cue for the -m- member reads the commonest noun in employment law as object concord

question: mwajiri anaposhindwa kukata NSSF kwenye mshahara matokeo yake ni nini
guards_against: kukata (the infinitive) -- 48 corpus rows with no object infix at all. The infinitive IS a valid host, which is exactly why it cannot also be a match on its own

question: mzabuni ameandika invoice yenye VAT 5 nailipe au nikatae
guards_against: nikataE (if I refuse) -- a bare `nikat` cue matches it. 6 of the 12 corpus hits for that string are this word

question: GN 605A inasema nini kuhusu mshahara wa chini
guards_against: kuhusu (the PREPOSITION 'about') -- 154 corpus rows, the single largest nesting hazard in this change. Requiring an infix BETWEEN host and stem is what separates it from kuNIhusu

question: GN605A ni nini hasa na linianza kutumika
guards_against: 'lini anza' (WHEN does it start) written as one word. Not a morphology hazard at all -- a question word whose tail is `ni`. Requiring a TENSE MARKER after the subject prefix is what kills it

question: kama mwajiri hakukata PAYE nani analipa deni la kodi
guards_against: haKUkata -- the `ku` is the NEGATIVE PAST marker, not the -ku- object infix. Found by the sweep against the first version of this patch, where an optional tense slot let the regex backtrack and spend `ku` on the object instead

question: mimi kama mwajiri nachangia kiasi gani kwenye NSSF kwa mshahara wa 800000 na mfanyakazi anakatwa vipi
guards_against: the new employee pattern must not steal a question that states the EMPLOYER frame. nssf_party tests employer BEFORE employee and this row proves the order still holds with a -katwa form present

question: jumla ya michango ya NSSF inayokatwa kwa mshahara wa 900000 ni kiasi gani
guards_against: a genuine TOTAL question that also contains a passive deduction verb. Precedence (total first) is the only thing protecting it, so it is pinned rather than assumed

question: nina watu wengi wanaonunua bidhaa zangu dukani je natakiwa kuwa na mashine ya risiti
guards_against: the `ongeza watu` payroll cue must not generalise to bare `watu`. That word is in 178 corpus rows and most are not about employees -- this one is a customer count in an EFD question
